His birth is celebrated by Christians in the tenth month after his conception; and from the eighth day before the kalends of April, when he is believed to have been conceived, to the eighth day before the kalends of January, when he is believed or handed down to have been born, 276 days are counted, that is, nine months and six days. Whence it is plain that Jesus Christ is perfect man as he is perfect God.

Whence he says: “No one knoweth … the Father, but the Son, and he to whom it shall please the Son to reveal him”; because the Father reveals through the Son, that is, through his Word. For if the word we utter, temporal and passing, shows both itself and that of which we speak, much more does the Word of God, through which all things were made, show the Father as he is; because he too is so, and is what the Father is as regards wisdom and being. For as regards being the Word, he is not what the Father is, because the Word is not the Father: for Word is said relatively, as is Son, who is not the Father. Christ, then, is the power of God and the wisdom of God, because he is power and wisdom from the Father, the power and wisdom, as light from the light, the Father, and the fountain of life with the Father, the fountain of life. Whence: “For with thee is the fountain of life; and in thy light we shall see light.” For as the Father hath life in himself, so he hath given to the Son also to have life in himself: this is “the true light, which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world”. This Word was with God, and the Word was God. And God is light, not bodily but spiritual; nor made light by being enlightened, like the apostles, to whom it is said: “You are the light of the world”; but that which enlightens every man: this is the wisdom of which we treat. The Son, then, is wisdom from the Father, wisdom, as light from light, God from God; and the Father singly is light, the Son singly light, the Holy Ghost singly light; the Father singly God, the Son singly God, and the Holy Ghost singly God. So too the Father singly is wisdom; and both together are one light, one God, one wisdom. But the Son “is made unto us wisdom from God, and justice, and sanctification”, because we turn to him in time, that with him we may abide for ever; and he in time was the Word made flesh, and dwelt among us.

31_marg1433: Rabanus. For so great a craving for images holds men that the things that are true are cheaper to them. They delight, namely, in gold and gems; their gleam dazzles the eyes. Without these they think there is no religion. In these, then, avarice and greed are worshipped; they believe the gods love what they themselves love, for which thefts and robberies and wars are committed, and they consecrate the spoils and plunder to the gods, who are very weak if they are subject to greed. For why are they thought heavenly if they desire earthly things, or blessed if they are in want, or incorrupt if they delight in those things for which the greed of man is condemned?

31_marg1464: Instead of which things, etc. Rabanus. Or the nature of the heavenly food is described, which bore the force of fire where it needed to, and melted at the heat of the sun; for it appeared white and small, and as if beaten with a pestle, like hoarfrost. Whence in the book of Numbers: “the manna was like coriander seed, of the colour of bdellium,” etc. Mystically, in the hail and fire is signified the hard rebuke with which divine Scripture torments sinners; in the heavenly food, the comfort from above with which it refreshes the just. The reprobate, then, are tormented by spiritual hunger, and the elect are filled with heavenly bread. Whence: “Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.”

31_marg1481: Rabanus. The people of Israel in Egypt celebrated the pasch at the Lord’s command. Hence he says that they sacrificed secretly, because they did it in hiding for fear of their enemies; where they also learned through Moses the law of the Pasch, which was to be kept thereafter, having for a time suffered the temptation of the reprobate, but soon freed by divine help. Likewise in the time of grace the servants of God, to whom the divine law has been given in the concord of the two Testaments, are sometimes hindered by persecutors from practising the Christian religion openly, but in the secret of the heart they always sacrifice to the Lord. Whence: “A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit.” And elsewhere: “In me, O God, are vows to thee, which I will pay, praises to thee.”
31_marg1482: He recalls that God struck the firstborn of Egypt, when the Egyptians no longer pretended as before, but openly pressed the people of God to go out, saying: “We shall all die.”
31_interl4009: elsewhere: that the just should receive both good and evil alike, singing praises to the Father of all
31_marg1483: Thy almighty word: the Son, of whom it is said: “In the beginning was the Word,” etc. Here he is named the arm and the right hand because of the effective might of the divine power. Then, by the ministry of an angel, he executed his judgements on the firstborn of the Egyptians, he who afterwards sanctified to himself the firstborn of the Hebrews; now too by the water of baptism he saves the multitude of believers and kills the multitude of spiritual enemies.
31_interl4011: because “the word of God is living and effectual, and more piercing than any two edged sword”. In truth and without any feigning he judges and orders all things
31_interl4012: so that neither waking nor sleeping should rest be given to those who for their crimes were to suffer everlasting torments
31_marg1484: For the visions, etc. This belongs to the divine goodness, which chastises sinners that they may refrain and do penance. But if they abuse the patience of God, they will be punished for ever without excuse.
31_interl4013: which took place after the burning of Core
31_marg1485: But the just also … were touched, etc. Rabanus. He recalls that after the killing of Core, Dathan and Abiron, the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying: “You have killed the people of the Lord”; and as the tumult grew, Moses and Aaron fled to the tabernacle of the covenant. To them the Lord said: “Get you out from the midst of this multitude, this moment will I destroy them.” And when they had fallen on their faces, Moses said to Aaron: “Take the censer, and putting fire in it from the altar, put incense upon it … and pray for them: for already wrath is gone out from the Lord, and the plague rageth.” Aaron obeyed, offered incense and prayed, and the plague ceased. In Moses is signified the law, which teaches men knowledge and the love of God; in Aaron, the manner of supplicating and praying. So when God is angry, if the law comes back into our heart, warning and teaching us to turn to penance, to make satisfaction for our offences and to entreat for our faults, the indignation will cease, and the Lord will be appeased and made gracious, as if Moses and Aaron were interceding. But if our hearts are hardened, so that we say God has no care for the life of mortals, and the like, it is plain that Moses and Aaron are not in us, namely the knowledge of the law and the fruit of penance, through which we could escape destruction.
31_interl4014: an interweaving, so that all things are found in each one
31_interl4016: that is, the unutterable name, namely the tetragrammaton
31_marg1486: For in the priestly robe, etc. The Hebrews assign the fine linen to the earth, because it is produced from the earth; the purple to the sea, because it is dyed with its shellfish; the violet to the air, for the likeness of its colour; the scarlet to fire and the ether; namely, so that the high priest may pray for the whole world. For the world is made of earth, water, air and fire, and these are the elements of all things. Hence the first garment is of linen, which signifies the earth; the second of violet, which shows the air, because from earthly things we are raised little by little to the heights; and this violet garment itself, coming down from the head to the ankles, indicates the air poured out from heaven down to earth.
31_marg1487: The pomegranates and bells set at the bottom show the lightnings and thunders, or the harmony of all the elements and all things interwoven, so that all things are found in each one.
31_marg1488: The colours named above are woven with gold, because the vital heat and the providence of the divine mind penetrate all things.
31_marg1489: The ephod, and the two emerald or onyx stones on top of it, covering each shoulder, are interpreted as the two hemispheres, one above the earth and the other below the earth; or the sun and moon, which shine from above.
31_marg1490: The girdle with which the priest’s breast is bound, and by which the linen tunic, that is, the earth, is held in, they say is the ocean. The rational they say is the earth, which, like a point, though it contains all things in itself, is veiled by all the elements.
31_marg1491: The twelve stones are the circle of the zodiac, or the twelve months. To each row too they assign a season, and give it three months each. Beautifully is that which is in the middle called the rational, for all things are full of reason, and earthly things cling to heavenly. Indeed the reason of earthly things and of the seasons, of heat and cold and the twofold mildness between them, comes down by reason from the course of the heavens. Hence the rational is bound more tightly to the ephod. And on the rational the logion, that is, manifestation, doctrine and truth, signify that there is never a lie in the reason of God, and that truth itself is shown to men by many signs and proofs. Hence it came about that we know the reason of the sun and moon, of years and months, seasons and hours, of storm and calm, of the winds and of all things, receiving wisdom from God and knowledge of the whole fabric from him who dwells in it and teaches it. Over all, the mitre and the violet band show the heaven; the plate of gold on the high priest’s forehead and the name of God written on it show that all things beneath are governed by the will of God.
31_marg1492: And to these, etc. The true high priest, Jesus Christ, taking the censer of human flesh, with the fire of the altar laid on it, that is, the soul with which he was incarnate, and with incense added, that is, the spotless spirit, stood between the living and the dead and drove back death, destroying the devil, “who had the empire of death”, so that whoever believes in him shall not die for ever. This mystery the destroyer already dreaded then. For he recognized the figure of the censer, the fire and the incense, and what kind of victim was to be offered by him who stood between the living and the dead; and the image saved them, but the truth has come to us. For the destroyer would not have feared the high priest’s garments woven of purple, fine linen and flax; but he understood the true garments of the true high priest, and gave way to them.
31_marg1493: In the figure of the high priest he foreknew that Christ was to come; but because he saw him clothed in flesh, he believed him not God but mere man. Whence: “If they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.”
31_marg1494: But as to the wicked, etc. Vengeance came upon the enemies of the people of God to the end, because they corrected neither their life nor their ways; for with feigned shows they pretended repentance, and therefore did not deserve forgiveness. Hence Pharaoh, when, afflicted with the plagues, he promised that he would let the people of God go, after a little respite returned to his native cruelty until he was drowned in the waves of the Red Sea. So the persecutors of the Christian name, if they persist in their malice, will feel in their punishment how strong the justice of God is.
31_interl4017: because it obeys the commands of its Maker and serves him in all things. For to this end was the creature created, that it should obey him in everything
31_interl4018: the incarnation of Christ, who enlightens believers with the light of the gospel and protects them from persecutors
31_interl4019: which signifies baptism, in which the faithful are saved and the demons drowned
31_marg1495: So we too must give thanks to our deliverer with rejoicing, saying: “Bless the Lord, O my soul,” etc. Whence the Apostle: “Pray without ceasing. In all things give thanks,” etc.
31_interl4020: of God; whence: “thou … wilt ride upon thy horses: and thy chariots are salvation”
31_marg1496: Note that for the enemies of God the earth brought forth flies and the river frogs, but for the worshippers of God the earth gave fruit and the sea the nourishment of flesh. For it is fitting that divine providence should provide food for its faithful through its works, but bring a fitting torment on its enemies through the creature subject to it.
31_marg1497: Rabanus. Those who cruelly mistreated the ancient servants of God who came to them were worthily punished, so that, dark in mind and hard in feeling, they bore the obscurity of darkness and divers pains in the body; how much more those who despise the servants of Christ and the preachers of the gospel. Whence: “Amen I say to you, it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.” And it is well said that they were struck with blindness, as those were blinded by darkness who wandered at the doors of the just man, that is, Lot, seeking the way through the door and not finding it; for he who suffers the darkness of error within is hemmed in on every side by the heaviest losses, because he does not know the way of truth and does not find the door, which is Christ.
31_interl4022: elsewhere: for they exercised a more detestable inhospitality
31_marg1498: For while the elements, etc. As in an instrument different sounds agree by tuning in the harmony of the melody, so the discordant elements, keeping the law of their nature, are bent to the will of the Creator; for he did not make a creature contrary to himself, but in all things agreeable to his will.
31_marg1499: Which may … be perceived, etc. Rabanus. For men and beasts passed through the depth of the Red Sea dry-shod, and frogs coming out of the rivers filled the houses of the Egyptians. Fire mixed with hail rushed down from heaven, and neither did the fire hinder the water nor the water the fire. But where the children of Israel were, they harmed no one, so that it might appear that the elements of the world served not only their own condition but the will of the Creator.
31_marg1500: The merciful and gracious Lord is always present to his faithful, whom he always protects and rules, whom he sometimes purges in martyrdom; whence “the furnace trieth the potter’s vessels, and the trial of affliction just men”. “Many are the afflictions of the just; but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.”
